overview: A storm off the Pacific Northwest brings heavy snow to the Sierra and Utah through Friday, with a weaker system behind it for the weekend. The Rockies get lighter snow Friday, then more systems arrive next week, including a new storm near Thanksgiving.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A low over the Sacramento Valley is driving moderate to heavy snow in the Sierra, with a winter storm warning above 4000 feet until 4am Friday. Kirkwood has the most, with 21" total and 18" on Thursday alone. The NWS is calling for more, 17 to 34 inches Thursday through Tuesday night. Expect a weaker system over the weekend with minor accumulations.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: A potent storm is bringing heavy snow to the Sierra crest and strong winds over the ridges through Friday morning, with a winter storm warning in effect. Expect a brief break Friday afternoon into Saturday morning, then another system arriving Saturday afternoon. Mammoth had 15" total, mostly on Thursday.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A Pacific Northwest storm is bringing snow to Utah's mountains through early Saturday, focused on the north as it goes on. Snowbasin has the most, with 13" total and 9" on Friday. The NWS is calling for more, 19 to 32 inches Thursday through Friday night. Winter storm warnings run through Saturday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Snow rates increase Thursday night into Friday, hitting mountain passes hardest, with a winter weather advisory for the Tetons through Friday night. Jackson Hole leads with 8" total, peaking at 4" Friday. The NWS is calling for more, 10 to 25 inches Thursday through Monday. Weekend snow showers are possible.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: A fast-moving system brings higher-elevation snow Thursday night into Saturday, with gusts up to 45 mph adding blowing snow risk. Telluride has the most at 8" total, with 4" expected Friday. Temperatures fall over the weekend, and more storms are possible through Thanksgiving week.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Strong winds hit the southern Sangres and I-25 gap areas starting tonight, with a high wind warning Friday. A quick system Friday night brings a few inches to the mountains. Wolf Creek has 8" total, peaking at 3" Friday, with blowing snow Friday night. Cool, unsettled weather continues into next week.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Cypress Mountain has 7" total, with the bulk on Sunday, but rain is forecast for much of the period. Whistler sees mixed snow and rain through Tuesday, with 2" total.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says a wet pattern returns to Northern California and the Pacific Northwest around Tuesday Nov 25 and Wednesday Nov 26, with heavy rain possible. Its outlook covers through Thursday Nov 26.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
